newsitem.title: JAPAN: Most TOCOM precious metals rise, palladium mixed.
newsitem.headline: Most TOCOM precious metals rise, palladium mixed.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended mostly higher on Friday bolstered by firmer spot market prices, although palladium futures retreated from early highs to end mixed in volatile trade, traders said.
Some months of palladium futures surged by their 24 yen per gram daily limit at the opening, but the white metal quickly retreated amid caution that prices were too high.
"Trading in palladium was just crazy. The tight physical market made prices extremely volatile," one trader said.
Palladium futures ranged from eight yen per gram lower to 15 yen higher. Benchmark April ended eight yen down at 605 yen.
Short-term palladium lease rates have jumped to above 40 percent, compared with the usual two to three percent, reflecting the extremely tight physical market, traders said.

"Supplies are really scarce around the world. It is fully possible that palladium prices will climb above $200 even if the Japan-Russia export contract talks begin next week," one trader said. Traders said PGM shipments from Russia under contract would resume in July at earliest.
Platinum futures ended higher on the heels of palladium.
Benchmark April platinum was finished six yen per gram higher at 1,391 yen.
Gold futures ended slightly firmer, with prices moving in tandem with the currency market and supported by stronger bullion prices, the traders said.
Gold futures ranged from one yen to seven yen per gram firmer. Benchmark April was closed up one yen at 1,289 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $345.35/85 at 0753 GMT, against $345.50/346.00 in New York on Thursday.
"Spot gold was supported by stronger PGM prices, with no other factors in sight," another trader said.
Benchmark April silver was finished up 1.8 yen per 10 grams at 181.0 yen. --Tokyo Commodity Desk, +81-3-3432-7431
